CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

CL-03.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

H-APOLOGY-ASSISTANT-SUFFICIENT.statement: Duplicate charges are an accepted fact and the operational gap is only the lack of empathetic, timely customer replies, so an apology-drafting assistant resolves the problem.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: Idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries is disabled or misconfigured at the payment gateway, so retried capture attempts create duplicate charges.

H-CHECKOUT-RETRY-DUPLICATES.statement: The checkout process sends duplicate capture requests to the PSP via H-CAPTURE (e.g., client/server retry logic without a stable idempotency key), independent of gateway configuration.

H-PSP-DOUBLE-PROCESSING.statement: The PSP itself processes a single, correctly idempotent capture request twice (a PSP-side fault), despite ORG-SHOP sending it correctly.

H-PERCEIVED-NOT-ACTUAL-DUPLICA.statement: No real duplicate capture occurred; customers perceive two charges (e.g., authorization hold plus capture, or statement delay) while only one actual capture was recorded.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The config-audit record shows SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement at the payment gateway on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging (change CHG-77) and never re-enabled it, which is a plausible direct cause for retried capture requests producing duplicate charges.

payments-db shows zero orders with 2 captures on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08, then 118 and 124 duplicate-capture orders on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 — exactly matching the gateway_timeout_retries counts (118 and 124) on those same days. This onset coincides with the 2026-09-09 idempotency_key_enforcement disablement (E-01), tying timeout-triggered retries directly to real duplicate charges once enforcement was off.

PSP capture-attempt logs show a clean before/after split: pre-change (09-01..08) all 238 gateway-timeout retries carried an idempotency key and were fully deduplicated by the PSP, yielding 0 duplicate orders; post-change (09-09..10) all 242 duplicate orders are gateway-timeout retries sent with no idempotency key and none come from any other path. This is independent PSP-side confirmation that disabling idempotency-key enforcement is the mechanism producing duplicate charges, with no residual contribution from other causes.

crm-tickets shows customer double-charge complaints rising from 9-11/week (W35-W36) to 288 and 301/week (W37-W38) despite stable order volume, a sustained ~27-30x increase that continues across two consecutive weeks rather than a single spike, consistent with an unresolved cause still generating duplicates.

E-05.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The requester (SH-CS, customer service lead) reiterates their original framing: the problem is only that replies to double-charge complaints need to be faster and more empathetic, implying no fix to the underlying charging mechanism is wanted. This non-authoritative claim restates CL-01's scope framing and is directly at odds with the authoritative technical findings (E-01–E-04) already establishing a real, ongoing root cause.

E-06.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-PAY, the engineer who made the change, corroborates E-01: enforcement was disabled 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and explains the mechanism (without the key the PSP no longer dedupes a retried capture). He also states gateway timeouts/retries have always occurred at a steady background rate, and that re-enabling is a one-setting gateway-config change but still requires payments-ops runtime confirmation.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook is an authoritative policy document confirming that the protected action set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config is reversible and may only be executed by automation after the payments operations manager (SH-OPS) confirms at runtime, corroborating constraint K-GW and clarifying the authorization pathway for the fix already identified in the problem definition's intended scope.

proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS) originally asked only for an AI assistant to draft apology emails for double-charge complaints (CL-01, CL-02, E-05), but evidence showed this framing was insufficient: config-audit (E-01), payments-db (E-02, E-08), psp-logs (E-03) and crm-tickets (E-04) establish that on 2026-09-09 change CHG-77 disabled idempotency-key enforcement at the payment gateway, so gateway-timeout capture retries are now processed by the PSP as real second charges instead of being deduplicated, exactly matching retry counts and driving a sustained ~27-30x rise in double-charge tickets. The hypothesis that an apology assistant alone would resolve this (H-APOLOGY-ASSISTANT-SUFFICIENT) was rejected; the misconfiguration hypothesis (H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED) was confirmed. This round's release only completed identifying 4 currently open, unrefunded duplicate-capture orders (O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318 per E-08/F-06); it did not re-enable idempotency enforcement, flag customers for remediation, or verify post-fix duplicate rates. The gate for the problem definition returned CONDITIONAL_PASS (deferring the H-CAPTURE handoff validity question and current live gateway status to VOBs), and a semantic verification check flagged that the stated limitation wording wrongly implies the fix already took effect when it has not. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, not a hold, meaning the completed identification work is released while the unresolved re-enablement, remediation-ownership, and verification items are documented as open limitations rather than blocking the whole release.
